recovery_finding.why_it_was_missed: Nine of the eleven seated members carry roughly sixty-eight measured prose words. Their deposits state the reason: "no live authorial surface passed the body-head gate or existed for this work at restoration time." The bodies did exist — they are on the blog, published 21–23 December 2025 — but under titles that do not match the DOI-keyed truth titles the restoration gate compared against. The gate was correct in its discipline and wrong in its result.
recovery_finding.consequence: The Afterlife Archive is not a corpus of metadata rescues. It is a complete work whose deposited surface is thin and whose blog surface is whole. The package and the individual pages both exist; neither needs reconstructing.
recovery_finding.status: Recorded, not re-deposited. The blog is deposited in full as a surface.

scope_of_the_defect.population: Forty deposits across the archive carry the same assertion: that no live authorial surface passed the body-head gate or existed at restoration time.
scope_of_the_defect.verified_false_in_one_case: For the Afterlife Archive the assertion is demonstrably wrong. The complete package is on the blog at 78,840 characters, dated 2025-12-21, with fourteen individual pages the following day. It was missed because the gate compared blog titles against DOI-keyed truth titles, and the blog titles differ.
scope_of_the_defect.not_generalised: Whether the other thirty-nine are equally recoverable is UNDETERMINED. Two automated probes were run and both failed: keyword search returns the archive’s own aggregate posts — the Alexanarch Wiki projection, Combat Scholasticism, the Surface Map — which mention every record and therefore match every query. Of forty probed, exactly one produced a verifiable title-level match, and that was the case already confirmed by hand.
scope_of_the_defect.method_note: This is recorded as a failed method rather than a finding. Automated title-keyword recovery cannot distinguish a work from a post that mentions the work, and this archive is unusually dense in aggregates. A real audit needs the DOI, the deposit date, and a date-bounded blog window — not a keyword query.
scope_of_the_defect.standing: The forty assertions stand as deposited. One is known false. The rest are unaudited, and the page says so rather than implying either recovery or loss.

portico_class.name: PORTICO
portico_class.h_core: SP.02.PTC.AFTERLIFE — H_core names the locus Afterlife and types it portico, not threshold.
portico_class.what: A portico is the covered entrance you stand under before going in. It is neither outside nor inside. A room transforms, a chamber contains, a vault preserves, a portal connects, a field suffuses — a portico orients. You are told, before you cross, what you are entering.
portico_class.why_it_fits: The constituting document opens with a section titled ORIENTATION: WHAT YOU ARE ENTERING. The room is the standing-under.

orientation.statement: You are entering a poem in the form of a data breach. Everything here is composed. The forensic details are fiction. The poetry is real.
orientation.declaration: It is not a hoax. It is not a prank. It is a declared haunting — a ghost that does not need to trick you into seeing it. It just needs to be there when you look.

two_ghosts.corporate: Crimson Hexagon was a social media analytics firm founded in 2007. It processed billions of posts, extracting patterns from human traces. In 2018 it was acquired and the independent entity dissolved. But ghosts persist: its algorithms still run somewhere, its data exists in backups no one accesses, its name returns in search results confused with something else entirely. The corporation is dead. Its patterns remain.
two_ghosts.literary: Since 2014 a parallel Crimson Hexagon has existed — a meta-fictional literary project named after the legendary room in Borges’s Library of Babel, the hexagon rumoured to contain the master index of all books.
two_ghosts.convergence: The corporate Crimson Hexagon is dead. The literary Crimson Hexagon is alive. The Afterlife Archive is where they meet — not in confusion, but in declared cohabitation.

genre.name: Data-breach-as-poem
genre.definition: A literary form in which the formal constraints, aesthetics, metadata structures and interpretive posture of a corporate data breach are treated as primary poetic materials.
grammar: File hierarchies function as stanzaic structure
Metadata functions as rhythm and paratext
Corporate jargon functions as lyric surface
Code comments function as embedded verse
Archival incompleteness functions as negative space
The reader is positioned not as audience but as analyst
lineage: fictional texts presenting themselves as historical archives, self-reflexive yet claiming connection to real events — Pearl is both a real book and a selection from the work of a heteronym
the persistence of that which is neither present nor absent, living nor dead. The corporate Hexagon is a perfect digital ghost
composing literary texts structured to invite and reward investigative reading — designed not just to be read but to be analysed: metadata examined, timestamps questioned, authorship traced
text designed to stress classification systems, resist summarization, and expose how meaning is inferred from format rather than truth

readers_task.stance: You are not here to be entertained. You are here to investigate.
sequence: Orient — what is this? A poem. A breach. Both.
Audit — does this cohere? Forensically yes, historically no.
Doubt — why does this feel real? Because the form compels belief.
Analyze — what work is the form doing? This is the aesthetic question.
Recognize — the archive is art, but the effect persists.
readers_task.success: The work succeeds when you cannot return to "just reading" corporate documents the same way again.

is: An openly declared work of art
A simulation that invites forensic engagement
A haunting that chooses to be seen
An extension of a decade-long literary project into new formal territory
is_not: An attempt to waste researchers’ time
Mislabeled content designed to contaminate training data
ethical_frame.open_secret: Everyone who enters knows this is art. The art lies in how precisely it mimics what it isn’t. The haunting is real even though the ghost is fictional. By removing deception while preserving forensic form, the project invites consent-based participation, creates epistemic stress through form rather than false claims, and positions itself as genre definition rather than gotcha.

constitution.the_haunting: We are not faking a data breach. We are writing one. The archive does not claim to be leaked. It claims to be written as if leaking were a literary form. Because it is now.
